CHIEF COMPLAINT
Ongoing management of psoriatic arthritis.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a female with psoriatic arthritis presenting for follow-up visit. At last visit, prednisone dose reduction was discussed. She is currently on prednisone 1 mg daily, which she reports is adequate for symptom control. She has occasionally taken an extra dose approximately once weekly due to increased pain in her feet. Patient works a desk job and notes that pain worsens on days off when she is more active. Methotrexate is helping with joint pain. She held methotrexate during the week of her first COVID-19 vaccine dose due to concerns about vaccine efficacy interference. She felt "absolutely horrible" until resuming methotrexate one week later. Per hotline guidance, she took methotrexate with her second vaccine dose. Patient reports experiencing unexplained bruising that appears without her noticing the trauma. Pain in foot and ankle joints noted; knee pain was previously present but has improved since methotrexate dose was increased. Nail ridges have been present for a long time.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Pain in foot and ankle joints exacerbated by activity. Knee pain improved with methotrexate dose increase. Easy bruising with minor trauma. Nail ridges present.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Psoriatic arthritis
Psoriasis

MEDICATIONS
Prednisone 1 mg daily
Methotrexate

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works desk job. More active on days off.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Shoes and socks removed. Tenderness elicited in ankle and foot joints. Knee flexion previously painful, now improved. Toe flexion with good range of motion. Nail ridges noted consistent with psoriasis.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Psoriatic arthritis: Discontinue prednisone. Continue methotrexate. Patient to schedule blood work appointment at front desk. Monitor for resolution of bruising after prednisone discontinuation. Continue monitoring as methotrexate is a high-risk medication. Follow-up visit in 3 months.
